name: Pindi Chana
subtitle: chickpeas blackened with tea and whole spice, with no tomato and no onion

ingredients.note: pomegranate seed; the sourness that makes it pindi

prepNotes: Named for Rawalpindi. It has no onion, no garlic and no tomato: the colour comes from cooking the chickpeas with the whole spices, traditionally in a muslin bag with tea leaves.
It should be almost dry and very dark, not a gravy.

steps.text: Boil the soaked chickpeas with the cinnamon, black cardamom, cloves and bay leaves until soft and dark, about 45 minutes or 5 whistles.
steps.tip: The whole spices go in the water, not the pan. That is where the colour comes from.

steps.text: Drain, keeping a cup of the cooking liquid. Fish out the whole spices.
Grind the pepper, dried chillies and anardana together coarsely.
Heat the oil, add the ground mixture and fry 1 minute, then the chickpeas.
Toss on high 8 minutes, crushing a handful against the pan, adding splashes of the reserved liquid to keep it moving.
Finish with the amchur, raw ginger julienne and slit green chillies.

storage: Keeps 3 days refrigerated and improves overnight. Add the ginger fresh when serving.
